label: Slap bass, popped, sampled, close and dry
audition_title: libsonare bass pop vs the sampled reference
_rig: Not through the cabinet the rack's amplified slots share. `profile.py rig --against bass_fingered,distortion_guitar,overdriven_guitar,bass_picked,bass_fretless,slap_bass` is the measurement: 16.7 dB per octave from a knee at 6350, where the three confirmed cabinets agree at 38.5 to 40.5 from exactly 4000, and the curve distance to them runs 21.8 to 23.8 against 13.5 to the confirmed direct bass. So there is no evidence of a rig here, which is not evidence of none - this rack publishes no amplifier stage to switch off, so no A/B is available from it and the answer stays unclassified.
_shared_with_program_36: The same measurement found something the rig question did not ask for, and every comparison against this slot needs it. Program 36 answers with the same sample set as this one and differs only in how it maps velocity: the two pooled curves sit 0.01 apart. Across the shared grid 5 of 35 renders are byte-identical, and every row at velocity 104 and 127 is numerically identical - the residual sits 26 to 211 dB under the signal - while at velocities 32, 56 and 80 this slot runs 5.7 to 9.8 dB louder than program 36 with a residual as large as the signal itself. Note 52 is the exception in kind rather than degree: there the levels agree within about a decibel and the residual stands ABOVE both, so those two rows are different content and not one sound at two levels. The two slots are therefore distinguishable, but only below velocity 104, and any measurement that compares them above it is reading one reference twice.
_notes: Every fourth semitone across the compass this program is probed on, 28 to 52, and no further. Both ends were rendered before the grid was written and both speak: the peaks run 0.372, 0.311, 0.237 at the low, middle and high probe notes, and the share of energy on the played key's own series is 0.997 or better at all three. A note outside the compass is left out rather than transposed, because there the reference is stretching a sample and a model fitted against it would be fitted against the sampler.
_velocities: Five. On a plucked string velocity is the pluck itself rather than a volume control, so it moves the partial stack as much as the level: on this slot velocity 32 sits -15.4 dB under velocity 100 at the middle probe note. The softest row is kept because it is the most distinct timbre the instrument has, not because the level is interesting.
_dry: Nothing to switch off, measured rather than assumed. Not one of the plugin's advertised parameters matches `reverb` with this rack loaded, and the render agrees: the note goes to the numerical floor within a fifth of a second of the key lifting, with no tail behind it. `dry` therefore has no section to act on and is left off rather than claiming an effect was disabled, which makes this a dry anchor.
_stimulus: A plucked string is stopped by the player rather than by running out, so the gate is long and the tail is short - the opposite of a voice whose interest is what follows the release. The free fall happens while the key is still down, -15 dBFS a quarter of a second in and -54 at six seconds, which is what the long gate is for: a decay measured over a gate shorter than the fall is a slope fitted to its own first moments. The key lifting then damps it to the numerical floor within a fifth of a second, so half a second of tail records the whole of the stop.
_calibration: From `capture.py calibrate` on this rack: the reference renders identically in real time and faster than it, the same note twice is bit-identical - so there is no round robin to put a floor under the loss - and the settle minimum is a quarter of a second. `realtime` is kept on anyway, because a note streamed late is caught only by `verify` and would otherwise be committed as a measurement.
_timbres: One, and the ladder is monotone above it, so this capture cannot move the voice past `voiced` however complete its coverage. The rack holds one slot per GM program, so there is no second of this instrument in it to disagree with, and `source_for` takes every timbre of a capture from one plugin, so a soundfont render cannot stand in as a second. What the reference buys is a measured target for `autofit` and `--diagnose` where the voice could previously only be fitted by ear.
_dimensions: The slot is a popped electric bass source. `decay` and its two stages are the dimensions a plucked voice lives or dies on, since everything audible after the first few milliseconds is a fall, and they are read off a gate long enough to contain one.
_dimensions_na: The exclusions as data, since a dimension argued only in prose reads as a gap. Coverage is read against `toneclass.canonical_dimensions`, which for a plucked string names every melodic dimension - it has a free decay, a two-stage fall, a damper and a dynamic range, and the stiff-string ladder means something - so anything not gated here has to be argued here.

dimensions_na.stereo: the slot renders dual mono: the two channels are bit-identical, so the width is zero by construction rather than by voicing

_identity: Which product this is captured from lives in the untracked sibling `bass_pop.local.json`. Everything here is the method. Re-capturing needs the overlay; scoring, fitting and diagnosing read `reference/bass_pop.json` and need nothing.
_slots: Slot identity is measured, never taken from a name or a position. The rack is addressed by MIDI channel; this program answers on channel 6, and it was rendered at its own three probe notes before anything else was written, reading 0.997 or better of its energy on the series of the key pressed. The same renders are what say the slot rings at all: four slots of these racks hold a sample that is at the numerical floor half a second into a six-second key, and a grid written for one of those would take every measurement on silence.
